en: Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Śākyas in the Kapiḷavastava forest together with five hundred bhikṣus, all of whom were arhats whose taints were exhausted, who had accomplished their task, completed what was to be done, and laid down the burden.

[The monks] had attained their own goal, exhausted the fetters of existence, and were well-liberated in mind through right knowledge. There, the Blessed One delivered a discourse on the Dharma concerning Nirvana to the community of monks. Furthermore, there the great Śākya and great Mahāśākya deities from ten great world-systems had assembled and were attending upon the Blessed One and the community of monks.
Then, it occurred to four deities dwelling in the Brahma-world, belonging to the retinue of Brahmā:

"Today, indeed, the Blessed One is staying among the Śākyas in the forest of Kapilavastu together with five hundred monks, all of whom are Arhats—as previously described—along with the community of monks. What if we were to go and wait upon him individually?"

"We shall praise the Blessed One and the community of monks with verses. Then, just as a strong man might extend his drawn-in arm or draw in his extended arm, so too did the four deities of the Brahma-realm vanish from the Brahma-world.
They stood before the Blessed One. Standing to one side, a certain deity from the Brahma-kāyika realm spoke this verse at that time:
A great assembly has gathered on the slope; the hosts of gods have come together to the invincible Saṅgha.
We have come here to see you.
A second deity from the Brahmakāyika realm spoke this verse:
With a mind made straight, O monks, they apply themselves here, like a charioteer taking up the reins.
For they indeed guard their sense faculties.
A third deity from the Brahmakāyika realm spoke this verse:
Having indeed torn up the stakes,
as well as the Indra-stake, the crossbar, and the moat,
they move about pure and stainless.
The young elephants were tamed by the leader.
The fourth deity of the Brahmakāyika realm spoke this verse:
Those who go for refuge to the Buddha do not go to an evil rebirth,
having abandoned their human bodies.
They wait upon the divine bodies.
Having spoken thus, the four deities belonging to the Brahmakāyika realm vanished on that very spot.
Then the Blessed One, having surveyed the entire assembly of gods, addressed the monks:

"O monks, this gathering of deities is indeed very great; O monks, this gathering of deities in my assembly at this time is indeed very great. Even those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas who appeared in past times—for those Buddhas as well..."

Such was the assembly of deities for the Blessed Ones, just as it is now in my own assembly. Furthermore, for those Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Awakened Buddhas who will appear in the future, there will also be such an assembly of deities for those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, just as it is now in my own assembly. I shall speak to you.
"O monks, I shall proclaim the names of the deities; listen to my words,
you who are self-benefiting and composed."
Like individual lions... majestic,
pure in mind, and stainless.
Pure and untroubled,
they have taken refuge among gods and humans,
extending even unto Brahmā; they are the destroyers of death.
There were five hundred and two learners,
and another hundred and ten, as well as many thousands more.
Some clearly announced the deities by name, even the Infinite One; all directions became manifest.
Having understood them through his supernormal knowledge and having observed them, the Buddha, the Tathāgata,
the Teacher, then addressed them.
The disciples who delight in the teaching.
The divine hosts have approached;
listen, monks!
I shall declare their names.
Listen with one-pointed minds to my words, spoken in successive verses.
Seven thousand yakṣas remain in the forest of Kapilavastu, illuminating it.
Vena, the inhabitant of Kailāsa.
And those who have come to this assembly, as well as those who share their sphere of activity, are possessed of supernatural powers and radiant splendor.
Possessed of beauty and renown,
they approached and paid homage to the assembly of monks in the forest.
The Sātāgiri mountain, illuminating the three-thousandfold world system, remains shining upon the forest of Kapilavastu.
And he also went to the assembly,
as did those who were his companions,
as described previously.
The six thousand [beings] from the Himalayas,
all possessing various complexions, remain there, illuminating [the world].
Vena of Kāpilavastu.
And those who have come to this assembly, as well as their companions,
are as described before.
Thus, these sixteen thousand yakṣas, all of diverse appearances, remain illuminating [the surroundings].
Vena, the native of Kapilavastu.
And those who have come to this assembly, as well as those who share their sphere of activity,
are as described before.
Viśvamitra, Pañcaśata,
Viśvadeva, and Maharddhika illuminate [the world] and remain there.
The forest of Kapilavastu.
And those who have come to this assembly, as well as those who share their sphere of activity,
are as described before.
The yakṣa Kumbhīra was a resident of the vast city of Rājagṛha,
together with a retinue of many hundreds of thousands.
He is attended by the yakṣas,
and they too have come to this assembly as before.
In the eastern direction,
the king, the great king,
the lord of the Gandharvas, protects.
Named Dhṛtarāṣṭra,
he always delights in dance and song together with his kinsmen.
And he too came to the assembly as before;
[he guards the southern direction].
The king, the great king,
the sovereign lord of the kumbhāṇḍas,
is named Virūḍhaka.
Accompanied by his kinsmen, he always delights in dance and song;
and he too has come to this assembly.
As before:
[Sand_15] In the western direction dwells the King, the Great King.
The king who is the lord of the nāgas,
named Virūpākṣa,
delights in dance and song.
Accompanied by his kinsmen,
he also came to the assembly as before.
In the northern direction dwells the king,
the great king,
the sovereign lord of the yakṣas.
Known by the name Kubera, he always delights in dance and song together with his kinsmen.
And he too came to the assembly as before;
Dhṛtarāṣṭra was in the eastern quarter.
In the south is Virūḍhaka;
in the west is Virūpākṣa; and Kubera is in the northern direction.
These four great kings, the illustrious guardians of the world,
protect the four directions.
Possessing great supernatural power and great strength, they too came to the assembly as before.
The servants of those illusionists were deceivers and rogues:
Māyā, Kiṭi, and Vikiṭi.
And Bhṛgu, together with Bhṛkuṭinī,
then displayed their miraculous powers in Saṃbahucaitrika.
And they too have come to this assembly as before;
these here are the Yakṣas, the Great Yakṣas, and the Yakṣa generals who are the leaders of the army.

They were as follows: Indra, Soma, Varuṇa, and Prajāpati, as before; and as in the case of Atānāṭika, up to Triphalī and Trikaṇṭhakī. They too came to the assembly as before. Sahabhu the Nāga also arrived.
Vaiśāla, Takṣaka, Kambala, Aśvatara, Prāpa, and Guṇa also arrived together with their offspring.
Saudāsaka Dhṛtirāṣṭra … the lordly elephants Airāvaṇa and Mahābhīṣma.
The illustrious Nāga has arrived for me...
and they too have come to the assembly as before.
That powerful twice-born bird of pure vision, having come through the air to the forest, forcibly seizes the king of the nāgas.
"Citra Suvarṇin" was his name;
there, Suparṇin granted safety to the Naga kings.
The Teacher brought him peace with his gentle and joyful words;
right there, he went for refuge to the Buddha.
And he too came to the assembly as before;
[the realm] was conquered by Vajrapāṇi.
The Asuras have taken refuge in the ocean. … … //
Sucitra, Vemacitra,
Prahlāda, and likewise Mucila,
as well as the hundred sons of Baḍi.
All are named Vairocana.
For indeed, Rāhu has approached Baḍi’s army for its welfare;
this is your time, O Great Hero.
[He went] to the assembly of monks in the forest.
And they too came to the assembly as before;
Varuṇa and Vāruṇī also [came].
Then Kṣaumā went behind him,
and the illustrious goddess Varuṇikā also arrived.
The earth and the divine waters,
the wind and the divine purifier (fire).
These ten groups of ten bodies, all of diverse colors, remain after having illuminated [the world].
The forest of Kapilavastu.
And they too came to the assembly as before—
Viṣṇu the god and Sahalī the god.
And Yama arrived… and the gods of the Candropaniṣad,
placing the Moon at their head.
The deities of the Sūryopaniṣad,
placing the Sun at their head and placing the constellations at their head.
Maghavan,
the possessor of all [powers], has arrived; Śakra, the destroyer of cities, has arrived along with the Mandavalāhakas.
These ten groups of ten bodies are as before. The goddess Sabhikā has arrived.
Jvaladarciḥśikhopamā, Ariṣṭikā, Romā,
Umā, and Puṣpanivāsinī.
The Carakas, with their girdles firmly fastened and remaining unshaken many times over,
as well as Pradyumna and Svātikā, have arrived.
For it rains down upon all the directions.
These ten sets of ten bodies are as before.
[The verses are: Śuklā, Kaḍambā, Karuṇā.
The one clad in blue arrived;
the foremost one with pure white hair,
clad in yellow, arrived.
The Sadāmattas, Hāritakas, and Miśrikas in great numbers, as well as the Śuddhakas and Rucikas.
The glorious gods have arrived.
These ten groups of ten bodies are as before:
the Kṣemakas, the Tuṣitas, and the Yāmas.
And many times Kṛṣṇa spoke [of them]:
Lumbinī, the most excellent Lumbinī, and she named Jyotis, with their own blessings.
The Nirmāṇarati gods have been attained, as well as the Vaśavartin gods.
These ten groups of ten bodies are as before;
indeed, these ten have attained mastery.
Each one is a Vaśavartin;
Mahābrahmā is said to rule over a thousand Brahma-worlds.
Sanatkumāra and Tiṣya, together with their sons who possessed supernatural powers.
And they too arrived at the assembly as before;
and behind them followed others.
Hāritī is the sovereign lady,
supreme in complexion and form,
surrounded by her sons.
She also arrived at the assembly as before,
and all these [others] have likewise entered.
The gods together with Indra, together with Īśāna, and together with Prajāpati—
even the monks have transcended this.
Behold this counsel of Kṛṣṇa: "Seize him! Bind him with passion! May it be well with you!"
Having surrounded him on all sides,
release him alive with loving-kindness.
Thus, there Mahāsena urged on his black army,
and he himself also turned back to join the fray.
Even when enraged, he is not master of himself.
Having struck the earth with his hand and made a most terrifying sound,
he then caused the god to rain down.
A mass of clouds accompanied by lightning.
The Buddha, having indeed understood them and having looked upon them, the Tathāgata,
the Teacher, then addressed them.
The disciples who delight in the teaching.
"O monks, behold the army of Māra advancing;
even they shall become practitioners of fervent exertion."
Having heard the Buddha's speech,
and considering him to be truly free from passion,
his hairs did not quiver.
And they too, having conquered in battle, fearless and illustrious, rejoice together with their disciples.
Those disciples are the sons of the Victors.
The Blessed One said this; with their minds satisfied, those monks rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
The intermediate summary verse: Varuṇas, Viṣṇus, Sabhikas, Śuklas, Śyāmas, and Kṣemakas.
The Mahāsamāja Sūtra is completed; it is indeed finished. Well done!
